positioning.brief_for_strategy: Nobody has profiled this market yet, so nothing here says which of this company's claims are shared with every competitor. Write from the material, and prefer the claims that carry a figure - those are the ones least likely to be interchangeable.

rivals.name: Kit (ConvertKit)
rivals.why: The creator-platform option a writer compares against when they want built-in landing pages, automations, and a commerce layer instead of a bare-bones tool.

rivals.name: Substack
rivals.why: The default first tab for anyone starting a newsletter from scratch, since it's free, has built-in discovery/network effects, and needs no setup.

rivals.name: Ghost
rivals.why: Where a writer who wants a full website plus newsletter (not just email) ends up, trading Buttondown's minimalism for theming and membership tooling.

rivals.name: beehiiv
rivals.why: The pick for someone optimizing for growth and monetization (ad network, referral programs) rather than Buttondown's writing-first simplicity.

rivals.name: Mailchimp
rivals.why: The incumbent many buyers already pay for from their broader marketing stack and have to justify leaving when Mailchimp's enterprise pricing and complexity outgrow a simple newsletter.

rivals.name: Gmail BCC + a spreadsheet
rivals.why: What a writer does before paying for anything: a Google Sheet of emails and a BCC'd Gmail send, until spam-folder delivery and manual unsubscribes make that untenable.
